route: /style-board/ (the style board: module table:grid, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: at 390 px the four-column size table runs past the right edge, so the Weight column shows only 'We' / '12 kg' cut at the screen edge with a faint shade as the only sign it scrolls, while short cells wrap word by word ('About / 2 / years') and make every row three lines tall.
findings.reference: Nothing on the competitor's phone pages is cut off at the edge; any row that runs sideways shows a clear cue that it moves.
findings.fix: In reference.css at max-width 600px tighten .block--table .table-block th/td padding (e.g. 0.6rem 0.5rem, first cell padding-inline-start 0) and set white-space: nowrap on the short value cells (td:not(:last-child)) so four short columns fit 350 px. Where they still can't fit, give .table-block__scroll[data-scroll="sideways"] a wider, darker right-edge fade.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: at 390 px the label column ('Detail') takes about 44% of the table, so the spec column is squeezed to about 20–22 characters a line and each row runs 6–15 lines ('Humid storage', 'Adhesive compatibility'), turning the 315-word table into a long, narrow strip of broken text over about 1,900 px.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone text runs the full content width in lines of about 35–45 characters (16px/26px body); none of its sections packs prose into a column this narrow.
findings.fix: In reference.css at max-width 600px stack the two-column .block--table .table-block: tr display:block with its border-bottom, th/td display:block, the first cell as a small bold label over a full-width text cell, thead visually hidden. Failing that, set the first column to inline-size ~30% (th:first-child, td:first-child) so the text column gets the width.

findings.issue: The 'Specification and consequence' column still runs about 110–115 characters a line ('Made from 90% recycled materials and available in 3 shapes: thong, standard bikini and full coverage. The water-'). The table still spans the full content width of about 1130 px, so the repair since the last review (.block--table .table-block__scroll { max-width: calc(70ch + 20rem) }) has not given a reading-length line.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps body text to a short measure, about 60–75 characters a line at 16–17px.
findings.fix: Check that the max-width rule reaches the scroll wrapper (its selector or the ch it measures against). Otherwise cap the text cells directly: .block--table .table-block td:last-child { max-inline-size: 70ch } with the table at inline-size: auto, so the spec column keeps about 70 characters beside the label column.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the m5 heading ('Toddler Sizes and Custom Size Runs') is set in a regular weight while m9's table heading on the same board is bold (DM Sans 700), so two table headings of the same level show different weights (same at 390 px).
findings.reference: The competitor sets every section h2 in one heavy weight throughout.
findings.fix: Give .block--table .table-block__heading the site h2 weight, font-weight: 700, leaving its fitted size untouched.

findings.issue: The header row of both tables sits on a 2px solid black rule (patterns.css .table-block thead th { border-bottom-width: 2px }), much heavier than the light row hairlines below it, at both widths. This goes against the treatment's own note that tables carry single light rules.
findings.reference: The competitor's facts carry hairlines only, with no heavy rules.
findings.fix: In reference.css set .block--table .table-block thead th { border-bottom-width: 1px; border-bottom-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary) 35%, transparent) } so the header keeps a hairline, slightly darker than the row rules.
